title: Microsoft SC-900 Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals
shortTitle: Microsoft SC-900 Security, Compliance and Identity Fundam...
summary: Exam SC-900 is Microsoft's fundamentals level certification in security, compliance and identity, and it asks for no previous hands on experience. It suits business stakeholders, new IT staff and students who need to understand how Microsoft cloud security fits together. The exam is multiple choice and asks you to describe services rather than configure them, so it tests vocabulary and concepts instead of practical skill. Passing it earns the Microsoft Certified: Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals title, which is a common first step towards associate exams such as SC-300 for identity and SC-200 for security operations. Microsoft refreshes the objective list from time to time, so confirm the current version before booking. This page is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with Microsoft.

beginner.definition: SC-900 is a beginner exam from Microsoft about security, compliance and identity in the cloud. The full title is Microsoft Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals, and the exam code is SC-900. The questions ask what a service does and when a company would use it. You do not have to configure anything, which makes this a good first certification.
beginner.whyItMatters: This certification gives you the shared vocabulary that security and compliance teams use every day. It shows an employer that you understand the main security ideas. These include the shared responsibility model, the Zero Trust model and identity as a boundary. Because it needs no experience, it is a realistic first goal for someone moving into security work. It also prepares you for the harder Microsoft exams that follow. It helps you speak with confidence in interviews and team meetings.
howItWorks: Begin with the concepts area, which explains terms such as authentication, authorization and the shared responsibility model.
Learn the Microsoft Entra area next, because identity also appears in the security and compliance areas.
Use the free study paths on Microsoft Learn, and read each module summary before you move on.
Make short flash cards for the many service names, such as Microsoft Sentinel and Microsoft Defender for Cloud.
Try the free practice assessment when your notes feel complete, then review every topic you miss.
Check the current objectives before you book, because Microsoft updates this exam from time to time.
beginner.example: Think of a company that moves its email and files to the cloud. The cloud provider secures the data center building, but the company must still protect its own accounts and files. That split is called the shared responsibility model, and it is one of the first ideas in this exam. Later the company adds two tools. One watches for strange sign ins, and the other keeps old records for legal reasons. Each tool belongs to a different part of the exam. By the end of your study, those names and purposes should feel familiar.
takeaways: SC-900 is a fundamentals exam, so focus on what each service does rather than on settings.
Free Microsoft Learn paths cover every objective area, so start there.
This exam is a good first step before the associate level security exams.

objectives: Explain the shared responsibility model and the Zero Trust model
Define authentication, authorization and identity as a security boundary
Describe the main identity features of Microsoft Entra
Describe the Microsoft security services for cloud workloads and threat detection
Describe the Microsoft Purview compliance features for data protection

chapters.title: Describe the concepts of security, compliance and identity
objectives: Describe the shared responsibility model between a cloud provider and its customer
Describe defense in depth and the Zero Trust model
Describe encryption and hashing at a basic level
Define authentication, authorization, identity providers and directory services
Describe federation and the role of Active Directory
Describe governance, risk and compliance concepts

chapters.title: Describe the capabilities of Microsoft Entra
objectives: Describe Microsoft Entra ID and the types of identity it holds
Describe hybrid identity and workload identities
Describe authentication methods and multifactor authentication
Describe password protection and password management capabilities
Describe Microsoft Entra Conditional Access and role based access control
Describe identity governance, access reviews and Privileged Identity Management
Describe Microsoft Entra ID Protection and how risk is detected

chapters.title: Describe the capabilities of Microsoft security solutions
objectives: Describe Azure DDoS Protection, Azure Firewall and Azure Web Application Firewall
Describe network segmentation with virtual networks, network security groups and Azure Bastion
Describe Azure Key Vault and how secrets and keys are protected
Describe Microsoft Defender for Cloud and cloud security posture management
Describe Microsoft Sentinel, including security information and event management and security orchestration, automation and response
Describe the Microsoft Defender XDR services and the Microsoft Defender portal

chapters.title: Describe the capabilities of Microsoft compliance solutions
objectives: Describe the Microsoft Service Trust Portal and the Microsoft privacy principles
Describe the Microsoft Purview portal, Compliance Manager and compliance score
Describe data classification, Content explorer and Activity explorer
Describe sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, retention labels and retention policies
Describe insider risk management, eDiscovery and audit solutions in Microsoft Purview
